Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1499
Claimant:
Annette Taylor
Adjuster:
Alison Sweeney
08/25/2023
First notice of loss received from the claimant reporting a low-speed head-on collision at a local intersection, with a
complaint of back pain and a request to open an injury file. Claimant is unrepresented and was willing to provide a
recorded statement.
09/03/2023
Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time
of loss. Assigned the file for vehicle damage inspection and injury review.
10/01/2023
Spoke with the other driver, who gave an account of the collision that matches the claimant's description of how it
happened. Requested the responding officer's report.
11/05/2023
Police report received and confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. Two independent witnesses were
identified and contacted; both describe the impact in terms consistent with the claimant's account.
12/11/2023
Photographs from the scene and from the vehicle were received and reviewed. The visible damage is largely in line
with the impact described by all parties.
01/08/2024
Vehicle inspection completed. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records, and
nothing points to any damage predating the start of coverage.
01/16/2024
Recorded statement taken from the claimant. Account of the collision was consistent with the first notice of loss, and
the claimant has repeated the same account in every conversation since.
01/27/2024
Medical records received for the initial emergency visit. Diagnosis is a back strain, which fits the kind and force of a
low-speed frontal impact. No prior treatment to the same body area is known from available records.
02/04/2024
Claimant attended physical therapy on a standard schedule. Treatment notes show steady improvement, and the
frequency of sessions has been reduced accordingly.
02/18/2024
Reviewed the injury file with the nurse reviewer, who agreed that the treatment course is typical for this type of injury
and that the reported symptoms align with the mechanism of the collision.
03/13/2024
Claimant reports most symptoms have resolved and is near the end of the planned course of care. Follow-up with the
treating provider is scheduled to confirm discharge.
04/11/2024
File reviewed and all key facts checked against the evidence gathered. Liability and injury appear consistent with the
documented collision, and the file is ready for settlement evaluation.
</page>

List the facts written on this page. Copy each value exactly as it is written: same spelling,
punctuation and date format. Do not add anything that is not on this page. Use "" for a missing value.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
